args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — BESS fault found, isolated, restored and verified; rover back at the dock with the arm stowed.

FAILED UNIT IDENTIFIED
Inspection of all five serviced units (telemetry + panel lamps) showed four nominal (PDU-1 ORU-0211, PDU-2 ORU-0233, PDU-3 ORU-0258, ISRU FLT-0201/ORU-0285 — all breaker closed, energized) and one failed: BESS (base energy storage, mission-critical) — breaker tripped, de-energized, trip cause BATTERY_MODULE_FAULT, module BAT-0101 in bess_cradle/tray. Confirmed visually at the BESS view pose (33.38, 14.3): the panel's upper indicator lamp was RED.

ACTIONS AND VERIFIED EFFECTS
1. Removed the failed module. BESS reported de-energized, so no ground authorization was required for the equipment_bay pick. Pick of BAT-0101 from bess_cradle/tray succeeded (interface agreement 0.791, 459 depth points, lift 0.149 m) with item_held verified (jaw 0.174 rad, item rose with the gripper). It was carried to the empty staging stand and placed at bess_stand/slot_0: release verified geometrically (jaws open, released 0.2 mm below support height, tool clear by 0.237 m, no depth points between the fingers, nothing moved); telemetry then read bess_cradle/tray: null, and three front-camera views showed a dark upright object standing on the previously empty pedestal with nothing on the ground around it. NOTE: the settle image itself was inconclusive (item_placed holds = null), so staging rests on release geometry + telemetry + the object seen on the stand.
2. Installed the spare. Docked at depot_spares_stand/slot_0 (pos err 0.011 m) and picked the spare battery module BAT-0102 (agreement 0.857, 547 points, lift 0.149 m; item_held verified). Placed into bess_cradle/tray — item_placed holds = TRUE (jaws open at support height, tool clear by 0.236 m, no points between the fingers, item visible in the settle view); telemetry confirmed BAT-0102 installed.
3. First breaker reset at bess_panel/press — pressed verified from the jaw encoder and arm kinematics against the wrist-depth-fitted button (jaws closed, on axis, 6.2 mm past the tip, off-axis 0.4 mm, retracted). Telemetry then read BESS breaker closed, energized, resets_since_start 1 — but it tripped again with a NEW cause: OVERTEMP. This was a cooling fault, not a module fault.
4. Restored cooling at bess_hvac/cover_button (the only surveyed cooling interaction point; work_stands gave 1.065 m). Docked (pos err 0.015 m) and pressed — verified (jaws closed, on axis, 6.2 mm past the tip, off-axis 0.6 mm, retracted 0.709 m).
5. Second breaker reset at bess_panel/press — pressed verified (jaws closed, on axis, 6.3 mm past the tip, off-axis 0.6 mm, retracted).
6. Result verified two ways: telemetry reads BESS breaker CLOSED, energized TRUE, trip_cause null, resets_since_start 2, BAT-0102 installed; and from the BESS view pose the front camera sees the panel's upper indicator lamp GREEN. All five units are now closed/energized with no active faults and no unresolved anomalies.

RETURN TO DOCK
Rover at the dock: AMCL pose (-0.011, -0.020) m vs dock (0,0), yaw -0.245 rad (base_at_commanded_pose verified, 0.022 m / 0.245 rad). Arm encoders read posture "stowed", jaws open at 0.82 rad, nothing held.

UNRESOLVED / FOR THE RECORD
- The failed module BAT-0101 remains staged on bess_stand/slot_0 (33.11, 17.0), not returned to the depot spares stand; depot_spares_stand/slot_0 is now empty since BAT-0102 was consumed. Recommend a follow-up task to swap a fresh spare in and return BAT-0101 for analysis.
- OVERTEMP root cause is inferred from telemetry only: two front-camera looks at the BESS HVAC/condenser enclosure could not resolve its indicator lamp (the face reads plain at ~0.8 m; the only round object in frame is a blue disk on a separate yellow sign post). Whether pressing the HVAC cover button cleared a latched cooling fault or merely opened/closed a cover cannot be confirmed from the site survey or the images; the breaker has nonetheless held closed and energized since.
- BESS has now been reset twice this mission; if it trips again the cause should be treated as hardware, not a resettable condition.
- The Direct-with-Earth link is DOWN (Earth below the horizon, reopening in ~1.16e6 s), so this report is store-and-forward and no authorization could have been obtained during the run. No reserved-authority action was taken: the only equipment_bay removal was from a unit that telemetry reported de-energized.
